page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting hyper-threading with two threads per core. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It has no local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32s_v7 demonstrates solid performance characteristics. Its single-core stress-ng CPU performance scores 2234.59, while multi-core performance reaches 31862.21, both placing in the average tier. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8), which assist in specialized workloads. This is reflected in its strong single-threaded gzip compression speed of 35.62 GB/sec and strong prompt processing speed of 186.24 tokens/sec for a medium 7B LLM model. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 43.89 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show 2352.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 181.75 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32s_v7 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a resource-efficient choice for memory-bound workloads without paying for excess compute cores. However, the lack of local storage means all storage operations must rely on external Premium Storage, which introduces network-storage dependency. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel training, though its AMX instructions provide decent CPU-based LLM inference. This server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis (achieving 51.24 million SET operations per second in benchmarks), data-intensive web serving, and medium-scale analytical processing.

Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high 8.0 GB per core memory ratio. The server lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Benchmarks indicate average to strong performance, highlighted by a static web serving throughput of 43.89 GB/sec, a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 35.62 GB/sec, and a Redis SET performance of 51.24 million operations per second. Supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, it delivers capable medium-model LLM inference. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive web serving.
